findings.quote: E)  A horizontal block in row \(r=5\), columns \(c=2,3,4\).
findings.reason: Block E overlaps block C at (5,2). Consequently, the five specified blocks cannot be torn out as disjoint intact blocks.

findings.quote: Thus after tearing out these \(5\) blocks in each \(5\times5\) cell there is no triple left anywhere in the \(n\times n\) square.
findings.reason: Even treating all listed cells as removed, row 1, columns 1–3 remains an intact horizontal triple in each macrosquare. Thus the asserted blocking property already fails for n=5.
This triple count is incorrect for n=1, when there are zero triples. This is a minor endpoint issue, unlike the substantive upper-bound failures.

reason: The lower-bound counting argument works for n≥2, but the upper-bound construction both overlaps blocks and leaves available triples.
unresolved_obligations: Establish the upper bound using a legal disjoint-block construction that leaves no available triple and uses at most n²/5 + O(n) blocks.
